item.title: Naira appreciates to N1,445/$ in parallel market
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira appreciated by N10 against the dollar in the parallel market on Friday, exchanging at N1,445 per dollar, compared with N1,455 on Thursday. Similarly, the naira strengthened in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), appreciating to N1,376 per dollar from N1,378 per dollar recorded on Thursday. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the indicative exchange rate in the official market improved by N2 to N1,376 per dollar from N1,378. Consequently, the gap between the parallel and official market exchange rates narrowed to N69 per dollar from N77 recorded on Thursday. Meanwhile, the value of interbank turnover in the NFEM fell by 54.5 per cent to $106.9 million from $235.04 million recorded on Thursday. The post Naira appreciates to N1,445/$ in parallel market appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Courage, Creativity and Impact as Indomie Heroes Awards 2026 Series Continues
item.description: Children make a difference in many ways, and the 18th Indomie Heroes Awards (IHA) 2026 Series brings some of these stories to the forefront. An initiative by Dufil Prima Foods , the series celebrates children whose actions demonstrate bravery, creativity and compassion. Tomike Adeoye presents this eight-part series which features 18 young Nigerians, sharing their experiences and the different ways they have made a positive impact. Courage, Creativity and the Power to Inspire With six episodes aired so far, viewers have encountered stories of children saving lives, helping others, overcoming challenges and using their creativity to solve problems. Each story offers a reminder that children can make a difference, regardless of their age or circumstances. More Stories Worth Watching Beyond celebrating these young heroes, the series offers families an opportunity to watch, learn and discuss values such as courage, kindness and responsibility. It also gives children relatable examples of how their actions can positively affect others. With Episode 7 airing this week, there are more stories to discover and celebrate. Catch the Indomie Heroes Awards Series on NTA (Fridays, 5:00 p.m.), AIT and TVC (Saturdays, 5:30 p.m.), Channels Television (Saturdays, 6:00 p.m. and 6:30 p.m.), Indomie Nigeria YouTube (Saturdays, 6:00 p.m.), BCOS and CTV Kano (Sundays, 5:30 p.m.), and Africa Magic Family (Sundays, 9:00 p.m.). item.title: Cody Campbell once again makes it about himself
item.description: Credit: Keith Inglis on X If there’s anybody who perfectly encapsulates the “get in there and make it about you” meme, it’s Texas Tech booster and oil tycoon Cody Campbell. Campbell has taken on outsized influence in not just investing millions in the Red Raiders athletic program to bring their teams to prominence, but throughout all of college football as well. He has been vocal in advocating for sweeping, transformational changes to the sport, particularly around the Protect College Sports Act and nationalizing television rights . But he has also rubbed others the wrong way with how he handles his business. He publicly clashed with former Big 12 commissioner Brett Yormark with complaints over Friday night scheduling. And he’s shown himself to be a bit overly sensitive as he threatened a Lubbock radio station with pulling players from interviews over a critical tweet from a producer. He also regularly positions himself as part of the program through his appearances and messaging, acting as more of an owner or general manager than booster. So when Texas Tech clinched a Big 12 championship game appearance with a victory over TCU on Friday night, it was no surprise that Cody Campbell found a way to elbow himself into the spotlight. The booster showed up at the postgame press conference to ask a question to head coach Joey McGuire about the team having the momentum of a runaway freight train and why he’s so popular. Full exchange between Texas Tech mega-booster Cody Campbell and head coach Joey McGuire as he sat in on the postgame press conference following a win over TCU. Campbell’s question: “So, with all the adversity we dealt with over the last year, everything we’ve been through, can you talk about and I because I’ve seen it, the love that you have for your players, the love they have for you and and for each other, and how that’s gotten us through everything we’ve dealt with and why we’re in the place we’re in once again this year?” — Keith Inglis (@KeithInglisDT) November 27, 2026 Naturally, Cody Campbell will say that he’s only doing this because he wants McGuire and the team to get the respect and love that they are due and it’s all about lifting them up. But in reality, he’s only taking the attention for himself once again. There is no reason for him to be showing up and asking questions at a postgame press conference. None. But because he is the one that’s paying for all of this, he can do whatever he wants. If Campbell really wanted McGuire and the team to get some shine, the best thing he could do is get out of the way and let them actually have the moment for themselves. But that’s something that he seems incapable of understanding. The post Cody Campbell steals the spotlight in crashing Texas Tech press conference appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Jackson Koivun Wins The 2026 Skins Game
item.description: HOBE SOUND, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 27: Jackson Koivun of the United States plays his shot from the seventh tee during the Farmers Insurance Skins Game at Atlantic Fields Club on November 27, 2026 in Hobe Sound, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) Getty Images Last year saw the return of the popular golf event call the Skins Game. What used to be a staple for golf fans during the offseason stopped abruptly in 2008 returned in 2025 for Black Friday viewing. This event brings together four PGA Tour pros to compete in a friendly but high-stakes competition with a total purse of $4 million dollars. The 2026 event had the following golfers competing for big-time money. 2026 Skins Game Participants: Justin Thomas Wyndham Clark Brooks Koepka Jackson Koivun The event, which took place at The Atlantic Fields Club in Hobe Sound, Florida, returned to its original format of the event. The competition, which started back in 1983, abandoned the “reverse purse” from 2025, in which each player started with $1 million and the amount went up or down based on whether a player won or lost a hole. For many viewers and spectators, it didn’t resound as much as the older format. The old format, for those who don’t remember, has each player starting at $0, making every hole’s value clearer and more obvious. Each hole carries a dollar value and tied holes will roll over, which can raise the stakes rather quickly. All golfers involved in this year’s event are first-time players in the Skins Game, but it was Justin Thomas who was slated to be in last year’s event before undergoing offseason back surgery and having to remove himself from the field. Unlike 2025, where Xander Schauffele failed to win even a single skin during the event, this event was competitive till the very end. This year there was a serious carryover down the stretch which resulted in an 18th hold worth $2 million dollars. No one could win the hole out-right, which meant they headed to a “19th” hole. The tee box was placed 118 yards from the pin on the 18th hole, and every player got a shot. Closest to the hole, while hitting the green, won the $2 million dollars. Thomas was up first, and missed the green long. Second was Clark, and he too missed the green, landing on the fringe. Koepka was third to hit, and he hit a safe shot in the middle of the green. The pressure was on the 21-year-old Koivun to put his shot inside Koepka, and the result was extremely close to Koepka. The result required an official measurement, which showed Koivun won the hole, and the event. The shot equated in Koivun winning $2.375-million, a total which topped his career earnings so far on the PGA Tour. When all was said and done, the money totals were as follows for the event: Jackson Koivun: $2.375 Million Brooks Koepka: $700,000 Justin Thomas: $475,000 Wyndham Clark: $400,000 The event was much more competitive than the 2025 iteration, and should be deemed as a success. item.title: Exclusive: Lakers’ Collin Sexton On Luka Dončić’s MVP Chances: “He’s Got It”
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Ed Szczepanski-Imagn Images The conviction in Collin Sexton’ s voice grew as he pondered the question. The topic: Has Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Dončić built enough of a case to challenge San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama for the NBA’s regular-season MVP award? “He’s got it,” Sexton told Fadeaway World about Dončić’s MVP chances. “He’s got it. We just have to keep doing our part. We have to play the right way, play as a team and watch everybody cook up.” The Lakers (15-3) enter Friday’s game against the Spurs (15-4) because of Dončić’s enduring dominance and the team’s strong chemistry. Dončić averages a league-leading 36.6 points per game while shooting 46% from the field and 36.5% percent from 3-point range. He also ranks seventh overall in assists (7.7) and steals (1.8) per game. The Lakers have also boasted offensive and defensive balance even with nine new players and Austin Reaves missing the past five games with a bruised left heel. That’s far too early to know whether that will be enough for the Lakers to supplant the Spurs. Wembanyama has also sparked regular-season MVP buzz for his defensive dominance (a league-leading 3.8 blocks per game) and offensive versatility (30.7 points per game, third overall). Following last season’s Finals loss, the Spurs have also leaned on their continuity and depth even amid second-year guard Dylan Harper missing the past four games with a strained left hip. No wonder this head-to-head matchup sparks intrigue on a potential Western Conference Finals preview and two-man race for regular-season MVP. Lakers coach JJ Redick , Sexton and other Lakers players have downplayed that storyline and the potential big-picture implications. That didn’t cloud Sexton’s optimism about Dončić’s MVP chances, though. Sexton also maintained optimism about his own play. After signing with the Lakers on a two-year, $19 million deal last summer, Sexton has shown various ups and downs in a reserve role. The good: Sexton has averaged 10.8 points while providing locker-room leadership with positive energy and hustle. The bad: Sexton has shot only 42.9% from the field and 27.9% from 3-point range while collecting at least four fouls in five games. That partly explains Redick’s recent talk with Sexton. “We had a sit-down conversation about just being patient. ‘You’re going to play, just be patient, and when you get in there, make the right plays and just continue to play within the realm of the team and be organized.’” Sexton said in a post-game press conference following the Lakers’ win over the Utah Jazz on Monday. “We’re organized, and that’s a big part of something I have to make sure I’m doing whenever we’re out there. Get a good shot. Make sure we’re not turning the ball over. And make sure that everyone’s in their right spots. item.title: Opinion: Why Doesn’t Arteta Play His Strikers Together More Often?
item.description: Opinion: Why Doesn’t Arteta Play His Strikers Together More Often? I am not a football manager or a football expert, and I don’t try to be, but I like to think I know a bit about football, having played the game myself for a number of years alongside being a huge football fan, watching many leagues and teams over the years, but most of all, of course, being a passionate Arsenal fan. Now, this may be controversial, but everyone is allowed an opinion, and I like to think, well, I hope, I know what I’m talking about sometimes. But what I would like to see is Mikel Arteta take the risk and sometimes play with two strikers up front. The rest of the formation and the way he decides to set up his team would not be a problem, but I’d genuinely like to see two up front. Why Not Play Havertz and Gyökeres Together? Now, I say this because, as we know, he seems to pick between either Kai Havertz or Viktor Gyökeres, and he rarely goes for the two of them together. But why not? If you haven’t tried it regularly, how do you know if it will work? Now, I don’t mean try it once and if it doesn’t work, give up. I mean give the two a chance to play together on a number of occasions! Everyone has their moans and groans when our strikers are not scoring, and yes, sometimes the delivery is not what it should be, but sometimes you have to take the game into your own hands and try, as we saw with Gyökeres’ goal against Borussia Dortmund the other night, which was a rather sweet strike. So why does Gyökeres seem to score left, right and centre for Sweden but struggle for Arsenal? There may be a number of reasons, but one reason I believe is because he is high in confidence, and more often than not, he is not playing as a lone striker as he tends to do for Arsenal. Sweden seems to have built their team around Gyökeres, and in the Nations League this year he has often played in a strike partnership, notably alongside Liverpool’s Alexander Isak, hence the great goalscoring form for his country. He scored six goals in five Nations League games this campaign and recently made history by scoring in eight consecutive matches in the competition , across two editions, scoring 12 goals during that run. Gyökeres is a player who can hold the ball up well and make that pass, whereas Havertz tends to struggle in that department depending on who is defending him. But he can offer good off-the-ball movement and good link-up play to the team. So why can the two not play together? (Photo by Richard Pelham/Getty Images) Could a Strike Partnership Bring More Goals? Gyökeres reminds me a bit of Olivier Giroud at times with the hold-up play and the running off the shoulder, but we know back in Giroud’s Arsenal playing days he had support from other strikers most of the time when he wasn’t deployed as a focal striker. I guess from the outside it’s easy to see what would or should maybe work, but surely it would have crossed Arteta’s mind once or twice, you would think, to play the two together

item.title: Section 1 moving forward with plan to separate non-public schools during playoffs, despite state objections
item.description: Section 1 is moving forward with a plan that would separate its public and non-public schools during postseason athletic competition, despite the move previously being overturned by a NYSPHSAA appeals panel. (Jim Franco/Times Union) When the Christian Brothers Academy football team takes the field Saturday night at Middletown High School for a Class AA state semifinal against Section 1's Mamaroneck, the Brothers will be doing so against a team from a section that is attempting to separate its public and non-public schools during postseason competition. A win Saturday in Middletown could also put CBA on a collision course for a state championship matchup next week against Syracuse's Christian Brothers Academy. If both CBA teams win their state semifinals this weekend, it would mark the second time in three years that the state title in New York's largest classification is contested between the two private schools that share the same name. First up for the Albany CBA squad is its matchup against Mamaroneck on Saturday at 6 p.m. The Tigers represent Section 1, which recently announced that despite objections from the New York State Public High School Athletic Association, it was moving forward with a planned change to its constitution that would separate private, parochial and charter schools from public schools during postseason athletic competition. That move would leave the non-public schools ineligible to participate in state playoffs. Section 1 announced the change to its constitution in June, following a 69-4 vote of member schools in the section, which includes Westchester, Rockland, Putnam and Dutchess counties. Section 1's four non-public members - Albertus Magnus in Nanuet, Ursuline School in New Rochelle, Keio Academy in Purchase and The Lefell School in Hartsdale - were the only four institutions in the section to vote against the amendment. Three of the affected non-public schools filed an appeal with NYSPHSAA, and in July a three-person appeals panel from the state association ruled to overturn that amendment. However, at its October meeting, Section 1 announced plans to move forward with its plan beginning in the 2027-28 school year. In a statement to the Times Union, a Section 1 spokesperson said: "In June, 69 of the 73 schools that cast ballots supported proceeding with the changes, exceeding the two-thirds approval required for passage. Section One's decision to move forward with amendments to its constitution and bylaws is a matter of internal governance and reflects the direction of its member schools." The issue of private, parochial and charter schools - dubbed "schools without boundaries" by NYSPHSAA - competing against public institutions in state championship events has been a hot-button topic in recent years. NYSPHSAA convened an ad hoc committee to address the issue in 2024, which ultimately adopted a plan to provide statewide standards for reclassifying non-public and charter schools based on performance. item.title: Alaves star heaps praise on Jude Bellingham ahead of Real Madrid clash: ‘He’s a great player’
item.description: Alaves star heaps praise on Jude Bellingham ahead of Real Madrid clash: ‘He’s a great player’ Real Madrid will look to extend their winning run to 11 games in all competitions as they take on Deportivo Alaves this weekend. Heading into the clash, Alaves midfielder Antonio Blanco addressed the media as he offered his thoughts on facing Real Madrid and what it means to him as a player. Blanco came through the ranks at Real Madrid, even making his first-team debut, with Los Blancos still holding 50% of his transfer rights as part of his €4 million move to Alaves in 2023. Blanco wary of Bellingham threat First and foremost, Blanco was asked about the prospect of facing an in-form Jude Bellingham, who has found his best form under the leadership of Jose Mourinho. Blanco has immense respect for Jude Bellingham. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) “We know he’s a great player, but we’ll try to stop him. Madrid have many top-level footballers. We have to focus on doing our job to get a good result,” he said (h/t Diario AS ). Blanco, who has rediscovered his best form after a difficult patch, is relishing a packed schedule that sees Alaves play three games in seven days across LaLiga and the Copa del Rey. “What we like is to play matches and if it’s for three days, then all the better. You’re constantly with the tension of competition. Besides, the Copa del Rey is also coming up, a very nice competition that we enjoy playing,” he explained. Confidence heading to the Bernabeu Deportivo Alaves will have a tough challenge on their hands. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Deportivo Alaves will face an intense challenge against an in-form Real Madrid squad. But Blanco believes his team can cause an upset. “We go with confidence after breaking a run where we were struggling. The other day against Deportivo we got the three points and recovered our DNA. We’ll see how tomorrow’s game goes,” he said. Finally, Blanco played down the significance of Alaves’ narrow 2-1 defeat at the Bernabeu back in April. “Better not to look for references. We know they’re in great form. In the top flight any team can complicate your life. You have to give one hundred percent from everyone to try to bring back the three points,” he concluded.

item.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
item.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration. Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities. "The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, said in the same statement. This news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess said that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons . "Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.) Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology launched aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025. Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece. "Orbital transportation and return form a new layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.

item.title: Agit Kabayel vs. Nelson Hysa, a new champ crowned and Mikkel Kessler returns: 5 things to watch this boxing weekend
item.description: There’s plenty to be thankful for this weekend in boxing. If you’re looking for a plate of action as diverse as the one you tucked into Thursday afternoon, then look no further than the next few days — including all the trimmings! We have a heavyweight world title fight, a vacant lightweight strap up for grabs in Russia, a returning world champion and a Japanese triple-header! Let’s tuck in. 1. Kabayel out to make heavyweight statement in Germany WBC heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel (27-0, 19 KOs) finally gets to show us what WBC heavyweight champions called Agit Kabayel fight like … The 34-year-old will have boxed just three rounds in 644 days by the time the opening bell rings in Dusseldorf, Germany on Saturday night, with unbeaten Albanian Nelson Hysa (25-0, 23 KOs) being the man tasked with testing what Kabayel is made of as a champion. Kabayel was elevated to full champion in July this year following Oleksandr Usyk’s decision to vacate his heavyweight titles . Alongside Daniel Dubois, Filip Hrgovic and Murat Gassiev (we think ), Kabayel is out to prove he is the rightful heir to the heavyweight throne, now that we are transitioning into the division’s next generation of stars. And he’ll attempt to do that in front of heavy home support in Germany. “Nysa can bang” is what everyone will be saying in the build-up to this fight, having a cursory look at his record. But at 42 years old and sizing up at 6-foot-5, he could prove to be tailor-made for a jubilant Kabayel homecoming. Agit Kabayel vs. Nelson Hysa headlines this weekend's boxing action. picture alliance via Getty Images 2. Cruz and Subkhankulov mix it for the vacant IBF lightweight title It wasn’t so long ago that Andy Cruz (7-1, 4 KOs) was the next best thing in boxing, turning pro in 2023 off the back of a sublime amateur record, glittering in gold medals. And listen, he still could be. But since losing a majority decision to Raymond Muratalla for the IBF lightweight title in January this year, some of the shine has been taken off of the Cuban. Matchroom refused to meet conditions to renew his deal, so the 31-year-old is out on his own as his 2026 bookends with another shot at that same belt. This time he’s off to Ufa’s Wrestling Palace in Russia, facing off against unbeaten southpaw Artur Subkhankulov (12-0, 6 KOs) for the vacant 135-pound title, following Muratalla’s decision to jump up in weight. Cruz and Subkhankulov met back in 2019 in their amateur days, with Cruz pinching a close split decision. But with more on the line in Russia this weekend, it’ll be interesting to see how this matchup translates into the pro game. Subkhankulov has flown under the radar since turning pro in 2021. It might turn out he is limited at this level, but with a hometown crowd in his corner, he’s well equipped to give Cruz an awkward Friday night abroad. Can Andy Cruz finally become a world champion? item.title: In-form O'Leary out to defy old club Bristol City
item.description: Reunion day at The Hawthorns as Max O'Leary and Jed Wallace both prepare to face their former clubs [Shutterstock] West Bromwich Albion goalkeeper Max O'Leary has been in the form of his life this season, rescuing the Baggies on numerous occasions with some outstanding saves to keep them right in the heat of Championship promotion contention. But it is one save he actually failed to make that has dominated the build-up to Saturday's meeting with his boyhood club Bristol City at The Hawthorns. Bath-born O'Leary actually made his professional debut at The Hawthorns in a 2-2 FA Cup third-round tie between Albion and City back in January 2016 as a half-time substitute for injured visiting keeper Frank Fielding. And, when Albion scrambled in a 95th-minute equaliser to earn an Ashton Gate replay, which the Baggies went on to win, the scorer who left him on his knees in despair was none other than home midfielder James Morrison, now the Albion boss. "Yes, he managed to score against me in my first-ever game," O'Leary this week told BBC Radio Bristol's Sound of the City. "And he's mentioned it a few times since." Morrison confident Price will 'heal quickly' After 13 years on the books at Ashton Gate, during which he made 179 City appearances and had loan spells at Kidderminster Harriers, Bath City, Solihull Moors and Shrewsbury Town, he finally left 11 months ago to join Albion. And, ahead of his first meeting with City since, which also involves former Baggies skipper Jed Wallace potentially lining up against his old club, it has all gone rather nicely for O'Leary. "A lot of footballers just want to know where they stand," he added. "Ultimately i got that answer and moved on to a new challenge, which was the best thing for me - and it's worked out well so far." James Morrison regularly reminds his Baggies keeper Max O'Leary of the injury-time equaliser he scored for Albion to earn a 2-2 FA Cup draw with Bristol City in 2016 [Shutterstock] After proving a key part of Albion's improved late-season rescue following Morrison's installation as boss, O'Leary's tally of only 18 league goals conceded in 17 games this season is the third-best in the Championship, bettered only by Birmingham City and Southampton. That included a key save in Wednesday night's 3-1 win at Bolton, which kept the Baggies 13 points ahead of the 16th-placed Robins. "He didn't have a lot to do in the first half," said Morrison. "But, when he's called upon, he's producing it, which is the sign of a good goalkeeper who's confident and enjoying his football. "That save probably won us the game. And he now just has to keep doing that. He's got nothing to prove, facing his old club. He's been a tremendous addition." As for the other man facing his old club for the first time, Morrison also had the time to mention midfielder Wallace, who was quickly picked up by City after being released in the summer. item.title: GTA 6 Officially Passes a Massive Sales Milestone Just 1 Week In
item.description: We might have to stop saying something sold like hotcakes and start saying something sold like Grand Theft Auto 6 . Rockstar's latest has sold about as well as we expected, with estimates after only one week putting sales at over 50 million copies . That number will only go up in the weeks and months to come, especially if a new GTA Online mode and a PC version are eventually announced, as rumored .

item.title: Jamie Overton's maiden five-for powers England to seven-wicket win over Australia, take 2-1 series lead
item.description: England produced a dominant all-round performance to defeat Australia by seven wickets (DLS method) in a rain-affected third T20I at the Gabba in Brisbane on Friday. Jamie Overton starred with a maiden five-wicket haul in international cricket as the visitors chased down the revised target to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match series. Having won the toss and elected to bowl, England made full use of the conditions to bundle out Australia for just 108 in 16.5 overs. Overton returned remarkable figures of 5/12, while Liam Dawson picked up three wickets for 16 runs to dismantle the Australian batting line-up. The victory also marked Australia's lowest-ever men's T20I total on home soil, adding to an unforgettable outing for England's bowling attack. Jamie Overton's maiden five-wicket haul dismantles Australia Australia struggled to build momentum after being asked to bat first, with England striking at regular intervals. Liam Dawson provided the early breakthrough by dismissing Mitchell Marsh for 11, while Overton took catches at mid-on to remove the Australian captain and Sam Harper, who scored 26 off 14 deliveries. Jake Fraser-McGurk attempted to provide some momentum with an aggressive 22 off 11 balls but was deceived by Overton's extra bounce in the seventh over. The England all-rounder then took complete control of the innings, picking up wickets in each of his next two overs. He dismissed Nikhil Chaudhary for 19 before removing Ben Dwarshuis for a duck to complete his maiden five-wicket haul in international cricket. Overton finished with outstanding figures of 5/12, including 17 dot balls, while Dawson claimed 3/16. The duo ensured Australia were reduced to 92/7 before the lower order was eventually wrapped up. Mitchell Owen offered some resistance with 17 runs, but his attempt to drag Australia towards a competitive total ended with a run-out in the 17th over. Sam Curran then bowled Billy Stanlake, leaving the hosts all out for 108 in 16.5 overs. Australia's 108-run total became their lowest-ever score in a men's T20I on home soil, surpassing their previous lowest of 111 against New Zealand in Sydney in 2022. It was also Australia's second-lowest T20I total against England, behind their 79 all out at Southampton in 2005. Additionally, the score marked the lowest first-innings total recorded at the Gabba in T20 cricket. Rain interruptions and Riley Meredith's three-wicket burst Rain interruptions reduced the length of England's chase, with the visitors handed a revised target under the DLS method. Australia pacer Riley Meredith provided some resistance by removing Phil Salt for five before dismissing Aneurin Donald, who had given England a flying start with an aggressive 32 off 13 deliveries. Meredith also sent captain Harry Brook back to the pavilion for nine, leaving England with a brief middle-order challenge. However, the early setbacks did little to change the visitors' approach. item.title: Guinea-Bissau postpones elections to 2028 over inadequate technical, material condition
item.description: Guinea-Bissau’s military rulers have postponed presidential and parliamentary elections scheduled for next week by nearly two years, further delaying the country’s return to civilian rule. Transitional President, Gen. Horta N’Tam, announced in a decree that the elections, initially scheduled for December 6, would now hold on November 26, 2028. The announcement came exactly one year after the military seized power, promising to restore civilian rule within 12 months. In a statement, the presidency said an assessment of preparations for the elections had revealed insufficient “technical, material and financial conditions” to conduct the polls as scheduled. It said the postponement would provide more time to ensure that the elections were credible, transparent and inclusive, with all candidates given equal opportunities. The presidency also reaffirmed its commitment to conducting the country’s first local government elections but did not announce a date for the exercise. Gen. N’Tam was sworn in as transitional president a day after the military overthrew President Umaro Sissoco Embaló in November 2025. The coup occurred three days after general elections and a day before provisional results were expected to be announced. Both Embaló and his main challenger, Fernando Dias, had claimed victory in the election. Embaló, who has since been living in exile in Morocco, was barred from returning to Guinea-Bissau last month, despite expressing interest in contesting the elections. Guinea-Bissau has experienced several coups and attempted coups since gaining independence from Portugal in 1974. item.title: Sporting JAX defender earns second Scotland national team selection
item.description: Sporting Club Jacksonville Sporting Club Jacksonville defender Georgia Brown has earned a selection to the Scotland Women’s National Team for the upcoming FIFA Women’s World Cup second-round play-off matches against Sweden. The roster spot marks the second international call-up of the season for the 24-year-old defender, who competes professionally in the Gainbridge Super League. A victory over Sweden across the two-legged aggregate series would secure Scotland a place in the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup. Qualification would mark only the second time in the national team’s history that it has reached the tournament. Brown was previously selected for Scotland’s qualifying matches against Czechia in October. Brown has started 11 Gainbridge Super League matches on the back line for Sporting JAX this season. She noted that representing her country offers a meaningful opportunity to compete for a World Cup spot. “It’s an incredible honor to represent Scotland; I’m extremely grateful every time I get to put the shirt on and the feeling of playing for something so much bigger than yourself is incredible,” Brown said. “And especially with the opportunity to qualify for the World Cup, that’s something every footballer dreams of, so it’s a really exciting time.” Brown explained that participating in national team camps contributes to her overall development on the pitch. She pointed to the daily standard of training with experienced teammates as an asset that sharpens her understanding before returning to club competition on the First Coast. “I feel like I gain something each time I go away with the squad,” Brown said. “The attention to detail and intensity of the sessions and games at camp helps raise my own level and improves my understanding of the game, which I try to show when I get back to Jacksonville. Just being surrounded by players who have lots of experience playing at the highest level allows me to learn so much about how they prepare for and approach games, especially during high-pressure moments.” Following the selection, JAX congratulated Brown on her call-up and wished her luck with the national team. Scotland will host Sweden for the first leg on Tuesday, Dec. 1. The squad will then travel to Stockholm to conclude the play-off series on Saturday, Dec. 5. >>> STREAM ACTION NEWS JAX LIVE <<< [DOWNLOAD: Free Action News Jax app for alerts as news breaks ] [SIGN UP: Action News Jax Daily Headlines Newsletter ] Click here to download the free Action News Jax news and weather apps, click here to download the Action News Jax Now app for your smart TV and click here to stream Action News Jax live.

item.title: Mike McCarthy’s daughter Alex Noel makes thoughts on Aaron Rodgers saga clear
item.description: It’s been a tough week for the Pittsburgh Steelers and head coach Mike McCarthy , as the team prepares to welcome the Denver Broncos to Acrisure Stadium for this year’s NFL Black Friday Game . McCarthy was on the receiving end of an Aaron Rodgers tirade after the disgruntled veteran quarterback went scorched earth when he learned that he was being benched. Following his unhinged rant on The Pat McAfee Show , Rodgers was waived by the Steelers . While McCarthy hasn’t directly responded to his thoughts on Rodgers’ interview, his daughter, Alex Noel, isn’t afraid to let everyone know how she feels about the entire fiasco. Alex Noel, who is an actor, model, and social media influencer, used her Instagram Stories to send a very clear message about her thoughts on the situation. MORE: Art Rooney II backs Steelers’ Mike McCarthy, rips Aaron Rodgers in scathing statement Mike McCarthy’s Daughter Has His Back View this post on Instagram A post shared by Alex Noel McCarthy (@alexnoelmac) On her Instagram account, which boasts more than 10.5k followers , Alex shared a story from singer John Vincent that praised her father’s integrity on and off the field. “Super Bowl-winning Head Coach Mike McCarthy is not just a great football coach, but he is an even better human being, and I’m extremely proud to call him my brother,” Vincent’s story read. She also reposted a message from Cowboys owner Jerry Jones that praised McCarthy for his time in Dallas. MORE: Mike Tomlin sounds off on Steelers ‘dumpster fire’ amid Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy fiasco Then, there were messages from FOX Sports NFL insider Jay Glazer and Steelers legend Terry Bradshaw, who both defended McCarthy and called out Rodgers for stepping over the line and lacking any class during his exit. So while Alex may not have directly called out Rodgers with her own words, the content she has been co-signing is a clear sign that she’s not loving the way Rodgers decided to go out in flames and his attempt to take her father with him. Aug 21, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy (left) talks with quarterback Aaron Rodgers (right) before the game against the New York Jets at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images It’s going to be interesting to see how the Steelers deal with this week’s off-field distractions when they take the field on Friday afternoon against the Broncos. item.title: Lions fan chokes out Bears supporter in vicious Thanksgiving brawl
item.description: The Chicago Bears got the better of the Detroit Lions when the two teams faced off on Thanksgiving Day, winning a thriller, 39-35. But a Lions fan got the best of a Bears supporter in a wild brawl that took place inside Detroit’s Ford Field while the game was underway. A Detroit Lions fan fighting with a Chicago Bears fan inside Ford Field. Instagram/@metrodetroitnews The video was initially posted on Instagram by Metro Detroit News and started with a Lions fan raining punches down on the Bears fan, who he is already on top of despite numerous people nearby trying to pull him off. After several punches, the Lions fan wraps his arm around the Bears fan’s neck and seemingly tried to choke him out. Detroit Lions fan putting a Chicago Bears fan in a chokehold in the stands. Instagram/@metro The two men fell to the ground a few seconds later but seemed to be in the same position. Then another fan wearing a black jacket appears to try and stomp on one of the fans before getting pulled away, at which point the video ended. INSANE FIGHT A massive brawl broke out between multiple #Bears and #Lions fans in the stands at Ford Field during today’s Thanksgiving game. Punches were being thrown everywhere, and one fan appeared to stomp on another. (Via @metrodetroitn ) pic.twitter.com/iKTqYFiDgv — MLFootball (@MLFootball) November 27, 2026 A man in a black jacket stomping a fan on the ground during the Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions game. It’s unclear what sparked the fight between these two fans. But the Lions and the Bears are bitter rivals, and this is surely not the first time fans of the two teams have resorted to blows. Brawls between fans at NFL games have been a recurring theme over the past several weeks, with multiple videos of these ugly scraps going viral every weekend. Apparently even on a day of thanks, Thanksgiving, some fans are unable to hold their emotions in check. A wild video surfaced late Thursday of an Eagles fan manhandling two Cowboys fans in a fracas. That came on the heels of Rams and Packers supporters going toe-to-toe on Wednesday night.

item.title: Italy edge out Fiji in Nations Championship at sparse Twickenham
item.description: Italy take on Fiji as the sides battle to avoid bottom spot – not that it could tempt many to attend the match - PA/Mike Egerton Italy ended their seven-match losing streak to edge Fiji 23-21, but the clash between the Nations Championship’s lowest ranked teams was watched by a sparse crowd at Allianz Stadium. Billed as the “Super Bowl of rugby”, finals weekend has struggled to attract interest with only 32,000 general admission tickets sold for day one, resulting in Twickenham’s top tier being closed. Acting as the curtain raiser to the fifth place play-off between Ireland and Australia later on Friday night, Fiji and Italy at least delivered a hard-fought battle that went down to the wire. Sumptuous second-half tries by Peniasi Dakuwaqa and Kitione Salawa propelled the Islanders into the lead, reeling in Italy who had established a 17-0 lead built on touch downs by Federico Mori and Giacomo Nicotera. Ultimately it was the boot of Tommaso Allan that proved the difference with the former Harlequins full-back landing a decisive 68th minute penalty to complete a 13-point individual haul. Fiji played some thrilling rugby in pursuit of a late victory but their execution was poor with a knock-on close to the line and wayward line-out throw important moments that cost them. Italy defended well and showed greater discipline to end a losing run that dated back to their historic victory over England in the penultimate round of the Six Nations. 06:45pm This weekend’s fixtures Today: Fiji 21 Italy 23 Ireland vs Australia 8.10pm Saturday: Wales vs Japan 1.10pm England vs New Zealand 4.40pm Sunday: Scotland vs Argentina 1.10pm South Africa vs France 4.40pm 06:43pm Man of the match Ross Vintcent “It was physical, full credit to Fiji. We wanted to end this tournament on a high for our families and everyone back home. It was a hell of a battle and I am glad we pulled through in the end. We have had a tough six months as a team and we need to get back to where we were last year. We have to keep building ahead of the World Cup. This will be a massive boost in terms of morale.” 06:39pm Analysis FT verdict Not to be that guy, but I did predict an Italy win in this game. Think I might have been on the only one of my colleagues to do so! Fun game. Andrea Bocelli is now blasting out at the Allianz Stadium. Shame about the crowd, but it should liven up for the Ireland game later. We’re told they’ve sold 32,000 tickets, which is still going to feel a bit weird in this cavernous arena. 06:34pm Full time Varney boots the ball out of play and Italy hold on to win 23-21. That is Italy’s first victory since their win over England in the Six Nations in March. Italy finish 11th, Fiji 12th. That is also a point to the northern hemisphere. Andrea Bocelli’s Con Te Partiro (Time to say goodbye) rings around the stadium to celebrate Italy’s win. 06:33pm 81 mins: Italy 23 Fiji 21 The throw from the lineout is not straight! We cannot finish on that one so Italy have the scrum. 06:32pm

item.title: Xavier 71 – 83 Virginia: Just please make a shot
item.description: I’m assuming he’s pondering all those misses | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was hard to determine what was more infuriating today: the announcers, the officials, or Xavier’s steadfast refusal to make shots that matter. Virginia is an extremely good team, but Xavier made it a bit too easy for them today. For a game that tipped off absurdly early, this one turned into a decent contest once it got rolling. That took some time though, and by the time X had warmed to it, the Cavaliers had done what they needed to win. If you don’t believe me, ask the announcing crew that seemed to be Virginia grads (or possibly Chance Mallory’s uncles). With 12:12 to go in the first half, Mike Nwoko (15/4/1) was called for his second foul. I say called for, not committed, because it was a bad call. It functionally changed the game. Nwoko was too much for Virginia to handle when he was in, but he would get only 40 more seconds in the first half. Xavier ended that first half in a 15 point hole. Nwoko likely wouldn’t have scored 15 in the first half, but he would have made a difference. For the game his +/- was zero. X didn’t get the chance to find out if that would have held, because he had to watch. But Xavier also didn’t help themselves. They were hideous from the floor (39.3%), from behind the arc (1-8), and from the line (4-8) in the first half. That is appalling shooting and has been the story of the season so far. For the game the team was hardly any better, shooting .393/.227/.621. You can complain about the refereeing, which I found to be quite uneven, but you won’t win any games being that pitiful from deep or the line. Xavier is 332nd in the nation from the line. Had they made just four more, this game would have been different. That would have been 75%. Had they made two more three pointers, still a pitiful 32%, you could add six more points. That’s an easy, easy , ten points that Xavier left on the floor. Toss in 9-22 on layups and, well, you get it. Which is a shame, because they defended well enough to win. The Musketeers forced 21 turnovers and pressured the Cavaliers into missing six layups. Virginia ended up scoring 1.1 points per possession, but that came largely on good shooting from deep (12-30) and is still hardly an insurmountable number. It is insurmountable, though, if you leave easy points on the floor all game. Xavier’s defensive pressure was fun to watch, but when they couldn’t get out and run or at least create in transition, they couldn’t score. Ruben Dominguez is adding nothing to this team Dominguez is here for games like this. His whole raison d’etre is making three pointers. He hasn’t done that this season and he didn’t again today. He played nine minutes here today and played his second game where he made so little impact that he didn’t merit an offensive rating. Add in a 13 minute 0 offensive efficiency against Iowa and you have three games in which he has been so bad he’s been nothing. That means in 31 minutes over three games

item.title: HUSKER Halftime Check-In: The Fight Is On, Can We Finish Again?: Iowa 10 NEBRASKA 7
item.description: Nov 27, 2026; Iowa City, Iowa, USA; The line of scrimmage between the Iowa Hawkeyes and the Nebraska Cornhuskers during the first quarter at Kinnick Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The halftime score is about as expected, but the road is definitely not being paved the way many Husker fans probably pictured it. Iowa 10 Nebraska 7. That tracks, even if it seems we usually own the early leads before things go sour. Yardage? Iowa 162 Nebraska 147 Again, it seems like we usually win these yardage battles while finding ways to lose the game. Here’s where it gets to the part I like. Passing yards Iowa 122 Nebraska 88. Um, that’s not great, but Iowa out-passing you feels more surreal than anything. And the Husker completions have been clutch, especially where Luke Lindenmeyer has been concerned. Three of his four grabs have been on 3rd or 4th down, the latter on an incredibly ballsy play call to extend the drive that led to their only touchdown. That finished on a 21-yard spurt by Jamal Rule who has run for 57 yards on 9 carries at the big break. And Nebraska has outrushed Iowa 59 to 40. Also, for the first two quarters, they are the team opening the bigger holes and winning the line battles for the most part. The Blackshirts have given up some chunk plays, but tightened in the red zone when needed to hold Iowa to a field goal. If the roles are truly reversing a bit, let’s hope the score reverses against recent history as well. Full recap to come following the game,

item.title: Team News: Alonso drops regular starter and uses potential formation change with Caicedo out of position
item.description: Team News: Alonso drops regular starter and uses potential formation change with Caicedo out of position Chelsea face Nottingham Forest at the City Ground in the Premier League in just over an hour, and the teams are in… If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. Chelsea feature in a rare Friday night kickoff today, and the teams for their game against Nottingham Forest are in. There are some interesting changes. Levi Colwill is dropped, rather than Wesley Fofana, as some expected. Danny Welbeck has also replaced Emmanuel Emegha in attack, with Estevao dropping out for Pedro Neto. Jordan Henderson also comes into the team. You can see the full team in the post from Chelsea embedded here: Chelsea have a variety of possible setups Xabi Alonso leads Chelsea training. (Photo by Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images) There are a couple of ways this could work. It could be a back three, with Acheampong and Fofana flanking Moises Caicedo who would be dropped into the back line. That would then mean Pedro Neto and Pep Chavarria at wing back; Romeo Lavia and Jordan Henderson in midfield, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer out wide supporting Welbeck up top. Or it’s just a back four, with Fofana and Acheampong central and Neto at right back. Or Acheampong stays at right back and Caicedo is a straight up central defender in a back four, Whatever it is, it means out best midfielder is now in defence – hardly ideal. In other news… Our predicted lineup for the game was pretty close, with one crucial difference. Pep Chavarria has promised Chelsea fans that his team will be more motivated than ever when they take on Nottingham Forest tonight.

item.title: Ohio State vs Michigan: Five bold predictions for Saturday
item.description: Bold predictions are supposed to be a stretch. But they have to be believable, too. Nobody wants a prediction that's just fantasy. And in the history of The Game between Ohio State and Michigan, there have been many unbelievable things etched into history. It could be the same on Saturday. Remember, these aren't things that you would believe can happen easily; even as a pretty good showing, they are bold predictions, things that would be beyond the norm, but still possible. I mean, who would have ever predictied Michigan running back Tim Biakabatuka would run for over 300 yards against the Buckeyes in 1995? Here are five for The Game on Saturday. Each one is a reach. Each one could happen. 1. Jeremiah Smith goes for 150 yards and two touchdowns Jeremiah Smith has never had a big game against Michigan. Eight catches for 75 yards in two career meetings. That's the quietest stretch of his career against any opponent. Saturday, that changes. He's due . Smith is coming off a 165-yard game at Nebraska . He's the Heisman frontrunner playing in the biggest game of the season. Michigan's defense is good, but Smith is better than any receiver they've faced all year. One hundred fifty yards. Two touchdowns. The breakout he's been waiting for. 2. Luke Fahey throws for 300 yards Luke Fahey's career high is 360 yards, set in a loss against Oregon at home. He threw for 259 at Nebraska , and 260 yards in his first start against USC on the road. A 300-yard game would be a great development for The Game. But here's the thing: Michigan's defense is built to stop the run. The Wolverines are No. 9 in the country in total defense, and their front is the strength of the team. Ohio State is going to have to throw to move the ball. Fahey has the arm. He's got Smith. And he's got nothing to lose. Three hundred yards. His first flag planting in the rivalry. 3. Ohio State's defense scores a touchdown Michigan's offense turns the ball over. Bryce Underwood has thrown six interceptions in nine games. The Wolverines have been careless with the football all season. Ohio State's defense has had its struggles, but it's also made big plays in big moments. A pick-six or a scoop-and-score would be the kind of play that breaks a low-scoring game open. In a rivalry game, one defensive touchdown can be the difference. 4. Bryce Underwood throws three interceptions Underwood has thrown six interceptions in nine games -- not terrible, but not careful either. He was benched at halftime against Penn State . He's playing through a lower-body injury. Now he's walking into Ohio Stadium, in his first start in The Game in the 'Shoe, against a defense that knows it has to win the turnover battle. Three interceptions is a lot. But Underwood has been turnover-prone, and the moment is big. 5. Ohio State wins by 20 or more Everyone expects a rock fight. Urban Meyer picked 17-10 or 17-14. SP+ says 31-12 , but nobody believes the computers after what happened in 2024 . Here's the bold call: The compute

item.title: CIF Southern Section Title Previews: Division 2-4
item.description: We just previewed St.John Bosco vs Corona Centennial, but there are three other finals that deserve your attention. Thanksgiving week is one of the best sports weeks of the year, and California high school championship week is a huge part of it. There’s a ton of talent and good teams in this division. Let’s break down the games. Division 2 Final Palos Verdes Sea Kings (12-1) Bay League #2 (3-1) @ San Juan Hills Stallions (11-2) Alpha League #2 (4-1) The Stallions avenged their regular season loss to Chaparral last week in the semifinal. San Juan Hills dominated the bracket’s top seed 35-14. It was one of the most impressive wins of the high school football season. UC Davis commit Maxwell Porter has 12 sacks on the season and he will need to get pressure on Palos Verdes star Quarterback Ryan Rakowski. Rakowski is a Nevada commit who has thrown for 2,585 yards and 28 touchdowns with only three interceptions. The Sea Kings put up 62 points in a win against Pacifica in the semifinal. San Juan Hills has made their post season run with back up QB Parker Armstrong. Armstrong went 13-15 for 169 yards and a passing touchdown against Chaparral. The Stallions will ask Armstrong to manage the game and rely on their defense. The Sea Kings want to turn the game into a high scoring affair. Porter is one of the best pass rushers the Sea Kings have faced all season. Defense wins championships, the Stallions will prove that mantra once again. Prediction: San Juan Hills 31-20. Long Beach Poly Jackrabbits (9-4) (Moore League #1) @ Villa Park Spartans (10-3) Playoff At-Large (Bravo League #4 Villa Park hopes to win their first CIF Championship since 1977 while Long Beach Poly is looking to win their 21st (the most for any program.) Poly coach Travon Patterson got the Jackrabbits back on this stage. Poly lost four non league games early in the season. The Jackrabbits have been unstoppable since inserting sophomore QB Trevor Scott into the lineup. Long Beach Poly still has the elite athletes that they are nationally recognized for. Cornerback Donte Wright is a five star defensive back committed to Miami and Juju Johnson is CB/WR headed to UCLA. It’s going to be a tough task for Villa Park QB Jacob Titchenal (2029) who has thrown for 2,492 yards and 23 touchdowns. In order for the Spartans to stay competitive, they need to control the running game with Coy Collins. Villa Park’s defense held an efficient passing offense Newport Harbor to 12 points and a physical San Jacinto to 14 points. Long Beach Poly is just a different animal to defend. Poly has forced five interceptions during their playoff run. Their defense will rattle a young Villa Park quarterback. Prediction: Long Beach Poly 37-17 photo by the the 562.org Quartz Hill Royals (12-1) (#1 Gold Coast League) @ Downey Vikings (10-3) #2 Gateway League: Downey beat #1 seed Chino Hills 10-9 in overtime. item.title: Sunderland vs Tottenham Hotspur: Match Preview, Latest Team News and Score Prediction
item.description: Sunderland vs Tottenham Hotspur: Match Preview, Latest Team News and Score Prediction Sunderland vs Tottenham Preview: Team News and Prediction This is not a glamorous fixture, but it matters. Sunderland and Tottenham have both spent chunks of this season staring at the bottom of the table, and both have begun to drag themselves out of the mess. Neither side is safe, neither side is convincing, and that is exactly why this game has weight. Sunderland were rooted to the foot of the table at the start of November. Four points from a 1-0 win over Chelsea and a 0-0 draw with Aston Villa have changed the mood, if not the league position. They are still in the relegation zone, but they are at least functioning again. That counts for plenty when the alternative is drift. Tottenham know all about drift. After five matches, they were bottom. A summer of spending had achieved very little on the surface, especially for a team that had finished 17th in each of the previous two campaigns. Since then, the picture has shifted. Their 2-0 win over Ipswich last weekend was a fourth victory in five Premier League games, and that run has pushed Roberto De Zerbi’s side up to 10th. Sunderland vs Tottenham match details Sunderland vs Tottenham kicks off at 2.05pm GMT on Sunday, November 29 at the Stadium of Light. It is a useful marker for two clubs trying to establish whether recent improvement is real or temporary. The numbers suggest a low-scoring contest. Sunderland’s five home league matches have produced only six goals in total, two scored and four conceded. Tottenham’s defensive record has tightened too, with their last three wins all coming with clean sheets. There is no mystery here. Both teams have improved because they have stopped giving away cheap goals. Team news and likely absentees Sunderland are without Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey again. Xhaka went off after four minutes against Chelsea with a calf issue, while Brobbey suffered a thigh injury in the same game. Dan Ballard and Romaine Mundle remain long-term absentees, with Regis Le Bris expecting both back in training around mid-December. Habib Diarra is also set to miss out with a hamstring problem. Photo IMAGO Tottenham should have Sandro Tonali available after illness. Savio is out again after suffering a recurrence, with De Zerbi saying: “It is the same injury.” Tosin Adarabioyo has recovered from a calf issue but missed full training on Tuesday, so he remains a doubt. Mathys Tel and Mykhailo Mudryk are dealing with ankle injuries and are targeting the Arsenal match on December 6, while Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert are longer-term absentees. One player worth watching is Luca Williams-Barnett. The teenager scored and created a goal for Dominic Solanke on his first full start against Ipswich. That tends to buy you another game. Prediction for Sunderland vs Tottenham This has the look of a tense, narrow game between two sides whose revival has been built on caution and defensive structure. Spurs

item.title: Liverpool have joined the race to sign world-class Premier League star
item.description: Liverpool have joined the race to sign world-class Premier League star Liverpool Tracking Lewis Hall as Newcastle Set Huge Price for Elite Left-Back Liverpool have made checks on Lewis Hall’s situation, with TeamTalk reporting that the club are actively monitoring the Newcastle United defender despite the sizeable obstacle standing in the way of any move. The 22-year-old has become one of the Premier League’s standout young full-backs and, crucially, Newcastle’s stance is emphatic. Hall is viewed as “strictly not for sale”, and it would reportedly take a fee “north of £66million” to even open discussions. That figure would move beyond the current world-record level for a left-back, which tells its own story about how highly he is valued at St James’ Park. Hall only signed a new long-term contract in September, tying him to Newcastle until 2031. That commitment has not quietened outside interest. Manchester United have retained their admiration, and now Liverpool are also in the frame as plans continue behind the scenes for future windows. Liverpool Enquiries Highlight Left-Back Planning According to the report, Liverpool “have firmly entered the picture and are keeping close tabs on Hall’s situation on Tyneside”. That does not mean a deal is imminent, far from it, though it does indicate serious appreciation from Anfield decision-makers. The reasoning is clear enough. TeamTalk states Liverpool’s recruitment staff have concerns over “the lack of progress shown by Milos Kerkez” since his £40m move from Bournemouth in 2025. Kerkez played the full match in the recent 4-0 win over Manchester United, but the wider view internally is said to centre on whether a higher ceiling is needed in that position. Hall’s profile makes him especially attractive. He is homegrown, Premier League-tested and still only 22. The report describes him as “Premier League-proven and one of the best of his generation”, which aligns with the broader view around the game. Liverpool are not alone in rating him, but their interest appears to be concrete enough for enquiries to have been made. Photo IMAGO Newcastle Price Tag Sets the Market Newcastle’s position under Matthias Jaissle remains very firm. Hall has “cemented himself as a cornerstone of the Magpies’ side” and they have no desire to lose such an important player. That explains the valuation and also why any genuine move feels more realistic in a later window, if circumstances change at all. For now, TeamTalk suggests “there is currently little to suggest a formal move will materialise when the transfer window reopens in January” and that any real competition for his signature is “far more likely to ignite next summer.” That feels the key line in the piece. Liverpool are doing what smart clubs do, gathering information early, understanding the player’s status and making sure they are well placed if the picture shifts. Hall may be the “dream target”, but dream targets often stay that way unless the selling club softens or

item.title: Mercedes set pace in eventful Qatar second practice
item.description: Gasly hit an advertising board after leaving the track [Getty Images] World champion Kimi Antonelli set the pace ahead of Mercedes team-mate George Russell in a disrupted second practice at the Qatar Grand Prix. Italian Antonelli was 0.127 seconds quicker than Russell on the medium tyre, as neither driver set a time on the soft compound because of two red flags that punctuated the session. Lewis Hamilton also came to halt after his Ferrari lost power, with a virtual safety car deployed so the marshals could come to the seven-time world champion's aid. The McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri plus Red Bull's Max Verstappen completed the top five at the Lusail International Circuit, with the trio setting soft-tyre times that were more than four tenths adrift of the two Mercedes. The first red flag was to clear gravel off the track after an incident for Ferrari's Charles Leclerc early on, while the other was to recover the Alpine of Pierre Gasly following a high-speed spin. Frenchman Gasly hit a marker board before beaching himself after taking too much kerb at Turn 14 in the middle of the qualifying simulation runs. The interruptions led to the second hour being extended by 13 minutes to allow drivers more time on track in the representative conditions. Hamilton also had a moment with Verstappen that was noted by the race control. The Briton was on a flying lap when he got too close to the Dutchman, who was on a long run. Verstappen said Hamilton had moved under braking, but the stewards decided no further investigation was needed. The second Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was sixth on the timesheets, with Leclerc leading Hamilton in seventh and eighth, 1.3 seconds away from Antonelli's time. The two Racing Bulls of British rookie Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson were ninth and 10th. Leclerc had to head back into the garage after spinning and going through the gravel when Lawson was just ahead of him at Turn Nine. The Monegasque driver said the car did not feel right, and the Italian team spent a chunk of time repairing the damage to the floor. Antonelli, who secured his maiden title in Mexico City earlier this month, was also fastest in the opening session on the mediums. Mercedes did fit the 20-year-old with the soft tyre in the first hour, but he failed to set a lap time on them. Drivers will be limited to a maximum of 27 laps on a set of tyres at the Lusail International Circuit, meaning teams will have to make at least two pit stops during the 57-lap grand prix on Sunday, which starts at 16:00 GMT. The decision is caused by concern over the integrity of the Pirelli tyres on the high-speed, 16-corner track. Laps to the grid, formation laps and any laps completed after the end of the race will not be included. Hamilton was told by his engineer in first practice tyre degradation was "much higher than expected" after highlighting his own issues. item.title: ECOWAS Speaker warns of levy shortfalls ahead of 2027 budget
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Speaker of the ECOWAS Parliament, Memounatou Ibrahima, has warned that rising public debt and mounting pressure on national finances could undermine member states’ ability to remit the Community Levy, urging governments to strengthen compliance ahead of the consideration of the regional body’s 2027 budget. Ibrahima gave the warning on Friday in Abuja during the opening of the 2026 Second Ordinary Session of the ECOWAS Parliament. She said the proposed 2027 budget was being considered at a time when member states were grappling with increasing demands for development financing and growing pressure on public finances. The Speaker urged national parliaments to intensify engagement with their respective governments to ensure regular collection and remittance of proceeds from the Community Levy. She also called on lawmakers to scrutinise budget proposals and ensure that public allocations addressed clearly identified needs and delivered measurable benefits to citizens across the region. She said: “One of the major highlights of our deliberations will be the consideration of the draft Community Budget for the 2027 financial year. “Indeed, persistent economic and financial constraints, characterised by mounting pressure on public finances and the indebtedness of our Member States, with the attendant risks to the remittance of the Community Levy, as well as increasing demands for development financing, require us to exercise particular vigilance and responsibility.” Ibrahima added: “I wish to urge our national parliaments to intensify their advocacy efforts with Member States at the appropriate political level to ensure the collection and systematic remittance of proceeds from the Community Levy.” She stressed that every budget allocation must be justified by its relevance and expected impact, while priority areas should be determined by efficiency, performance and tangible results for the people. The Speaker said the Parliament would also receive country reports and consider findings from oversight missions covering goods in transit, the ECOWAS Mission in The Gambia, regional agricultural projects and the development of a climate-friendly electricity market. She pledged to work with the new President of the ECOWAS Commission, Gen. Birame Diop, and other community institutions to advance regional integration. Ibrahima also referenced the Lungi Declaration, through which regional leaders reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the legislative and oversight functions of the ECOWAS Parliament. She congratulated Cabo Verde’s President, José Maria Neves, on his re-election and called for peaceful elections in The Gambia and Nigeria, whose presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled for January 16, 2027. In his remarks, Diop warned that terrorism spreading from the Sahel continued to pose a threat to countries in the coastal region. item.title: Man Utd trigger Fernandes’ one-year contract extension
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United have activated a one-year option in captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract, keeping him at the club until 2028. According to the BBC, the option prevents overseas clubs from approaching the Portugal international over a pre-contract agreement when the transfer window opens on January 1. Fernandes’ previous contract was due to expire next summer. Fernandes, 32, and United are understood to have agreed to resume talks over a longer-term deal later, with their immediate focus on improving the club’s league position. The midfielder confirmed on Tuesday that contract discussions had been paused. United have been negotiating with Fernandes since the summer. He has turned down two offers, including the club’s initial proposal, but said the priority should be returning to winning ways. “I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games,” he said. Fernandes joined United from Sporting in January 2020 for £47m. He has since made 343 appearances, scoring 115 goals. Last season, he broke the Premier League assists record and won the individual player of the year awards as United finished third. United were open to selling him in the summer of 2025, when Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal made a substantial offer. After discussing the situation with his wife, Fernandes chose to stay, though he later said it “hurt” that the club had been willing to sell him. The captain has said he remains ambitious to win major honours at United. “My aim will always be to win the Premier League and the Champions League within the club I am,” he said. Fernandes is a doubt for Saturday’s Premier League match against Brentford after returning from the Champions League trip to Sporting with a virus. He scored both goals in United’s 2-2 draw with his former club but missed training on Friday. “We are going to assess during the day and then tomorrow see how he is when he wakes up,” head coach Mauricio Pochettino said. “We are not going to take any risks.” The post Man Utd trigger Fernandes’ one-year contract extension appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Wike’s Imo campaign demand an insult, says RHGN leader
item.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka The Deputy National Leader (South-East) of Renewed Hope for Greater Nigeria (RHGN), Mazi Franklin Ngoforo, has described as an insult to the people of Imo State and the South-East a reported request by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, to lead President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign in the state. Ngoforo, an indigene of Imo State, said Wike’s reported demand suggested that the state lacked the political capacity and leadership structures to determine its own political direction. He questioned why a political figure from outside Imo would seek to take charge of the president’s re-election campaign in a state with a history of producing prominent national figures and successful entrepreneurs. Ngoforo, in a statement, alleged that Wike’s political ambition reflected a desire to dominate and control political affairs in the South-East rather than build genuine partnerships with the people. He warned against what he described as attempts by outsiders to assume the role of colonial masters over the region’s political space. The RHGN leader maintained that Imo State possessed the political maturity, leadership capacity and grassroots structures to determine its electoral choices without external control. He insisted that no individual could claim ownership of the state’s political destiny. Ngoforo, however, expressed confidence that President Tinubu would secure re-election in Imo State in 2027, citing the mobilisation capacity of RHGN across the state. He said members of the organisation were already engaging communities and voters, taking the Renewed Hope message to the grassroots and building support for the President. The post Wike’s Imo campaign demand an insult, says RHGN leader appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: GTA 6 Players Are Not, In Fact, Eating Good
item.description: There are countless ways to spend your time in Grand Theft Auto 6 . You can steal an elderly woman's mobility scooter and go to a yard sale to find cool vintage T-shirts . But sadly, one thing you cannot do is savor a delicious meal, whether it's on a solo outing or even on a date night with Jason and Lucia. Bahreini discusses the aftermath of the January 2026 protests, the authorities' efforts to equate peaceful dissent with treason and espionage, and the extrajudicial killings of peaceful protesters. item.title: Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters , as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains. Chainalysis and Elliptic estimate that more than $600 million of the stolen crypto has passed through THORChain, though Elliptic said that figure could count funds that went through more than once. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned as much as $1 million in fees from the swaps. Separately, $342 million has moved through a coinjoin service mostly coordinated by a pseudonymous figure named Kruw, Elliptic said. A coinjoin combines coins from many users into a single transaction, so their origin is no longer visible on the blockchain. Elliptic has said the launderers will still need other services, such as over-the-counter brokers, to turn the coins into cash. The FBI on Oct. 31 published
