item.title: N450bn rice fund: Atiku asks Tinubu, ‘Where are the farmers, where are the mills?’
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain how his administration’s claimed N450 billion investment in rice production is benefiting local farmers, as more than 90 rice mills have reportedly shut down and an importer was allegedly granted concessions to bring in 150,000 metric tonnes of brown rice. Atiku said the developments raised serious questions about the government’s commitment to local rice production, particularly when farmers were struggling with rising production costs and mill operators were reportedly shutting down because of inadequate supplies of locally grown paddy. In a statement on Friday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, accused the Tinubu administration of using impressive spending figures to mask the difficulties confronting the rice industry. “This is the Tinubu government’s familiar trick: announce a fortune, hide the failure, and call anyone who asks for the receipts ungrateful. Nigerians are tired of being manipulated. “Show the farmers who received the money. Show the mills that reopened. Explain the import concession. Until then, the N450 billion claim is propaganda dressed up as a harvest,” he said. Atiku demanded that the government account for the claimed N450 billion intervention, which he said comprised N250 billion for smallholder farmers and N200 billion for a guaranteed minimum price programme. He questioned how much of the money had actually been disbursed, who benefited and what quantities of locally produced rice had been purchased under the programme. “Committed is a convenient word for a campaign. Farmers need to know what was disbursed, who received it, what produce was purchased and what price was paid,” he said. The former vice president also cited reports that more than 90 of Nigeria’s 260 integrated rice mills had shut down amid shortages of locally produced paddy, rising operating costs and competition from cheaper imported rice. “These are livelihoods disappearing: farmers without dependable buyers, workers without jobs and investors watching expensive machinery stand idle. No presidential campaign can wave away that wreckage with a press release,” he said. He said farmers in Kano, Kebbi, Katsina and other parts of the country were already battling insecurity and soaring fertiliser and diesel costs, warning that cheaper imports could further undermine local production and investment. “We built the mills. We grow the grain. We will not accept a future in which Nigerian farmers lose their livelihoods while the government celebrates imports as progress,” he said. item.title: EPL: Arsenal cannot take advantage of Man City’s poor form for granted – Arteta
item.description: Mikel Arteta insisted Friday that Arsenal will not underestimate spluttering Manchester City in Sunday’s crucial clash with their Premier League title rivals. Arteta’s leaders are six points clear of third-placed City heading into the showdown at the Emirates Stadium. City led the table in the opening months of the season before suffering a major dip in recent weeks. Enzo Maresca’s men have only won just in their last seven games in all competitions and are without a victory in their last four league matches. Arteta cannot explain City’s stumble but he has no intention of taking three points for granted against them. “I don’t know, that’s a question for them. All I can say is when I watch them play, a lot of the games they have to win they do more than the opponent, but this is football,” the Arsenal manager told reporters on Friday. “When we play the home games against big teams that becomes crucial in the title challenge, we know how important those games are. But the second part, we’re in November, and we still have long to play. “The challenge is for us, we cannot control what other opponents are going to do.” City boss Maresca has been criticised for his team’s poor form but Arteta is a firm admirer of the Italian, who is in his first season in charge after replacing Pep Guardiola. “I know Enzo personally and he’s a phenomenal guy. He lives and breathes football, is very analytical. He is already on the great managerial career already. Everything is super positive,” Arteta said. – Arsenal ‘hunger’ – Arsenal sit top despite also being below their peak form in recent weeks. They were held to draws in their last two games against Newcastle in the Premier League and Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League. Prior to that, the Gunners eked out three wins by a one-goal margin and suffered an embarrassing League Cup exit at fourth-tier Fleetwood. Arteta believes Arsenal are still rounding into form and he hopes the motivation of a valuable victory against City will spur them on as they chase the high of a second successive title. “Yes, more hunger to do it again. To have those moments again together,” he said. “Everybody puts in unbelievable shifts every week, to analyse the opponent, to breathe the right atmosphere around the boys and to win the game, week in, week out.” City’s dynastic run under Guardiola is an inspiration to Arteta even if they have lost their way lately. “You certainly learn from that. And that inspires you to go to a different level, and that’s the level Manchester City brought to this league, because what they have done is unprecedented,” he said. Arteta revealed David Raya is back in training after missing the Dortmund game with a shoulder injury suffered against Newcastle. Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised against Dortmund but Arteta would not reveal if Raya is ready to return to action this weekend. The post EPL: Arsenal cannot take advantage of Man City’s poor form for granted – Arteta appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Osun LG Crisis Will Be Fully Resolved In The Next One Week — Gov Adeleke
item.description: Governor Ademola Adeleke has assured the people of Osun State that the protracted local government crisis in the state will be resolved within the next week, following President Bola Tinubu’s intervention. Governor Adeleke gave this assurance in his inaugural speech during his second-term inauguration held at Osogbo City Stadium, where he listed some of the priorities of his second-term administration across all sectors. “I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter and in the next one week, the crisis will be fully resolved. Once this is done, our administration will ensure the rehabilitation of the remaining 102 primary health care centres,” he said. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke was sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. As part of his priorities, the re-elected governor promised to set up the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission, as well as infrastructural expansion and recruitment of teachers and rehabilitation of schools, including reviving technical colleges. He also said that job and wealth creation will be at the heart of his second term. “We will establish a digital hub in each of our three senatorial districts. This is to drive job creation in the digital economy,” Adeleke said. “In education, we will recruit more teachers and speed up school rehabilitation. We will expand bursaries and scholarships, keep tuition affordable, tackle cultism, and revive our technical colleges.” In the health sector, he said about 70 per cent of existing primary health care centres were rehabilitated and equipped with solar and power facilities in his first term. “We upgraded and completed 232 out of 332 primary health care centres. The plan was to complete the whole 332 PHCs, but the seizure of local government allocations halted the process,” the governor said. “My government made sure that our primary school teachers, healthcare professionals at our primary healthcare centres, and local government retirees got paid in the last two years.” Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke sworn in as governor for a second term on November 27, 2026. Photo: Femi Ojomo/Channels Television. Adeleke said his vision is to move Osun from a civil service economy to an industrialised one, noting that his administration is open to partnership with private organisations and economic advisory groups. “Specifically, we will target agro-processing factories, industrial parks across districts, free trade zones, sports and tourism development, and a better business environment. “Fellow citizens, we must heal the wounds of the past and unite for our collective good. I charge the Osun political class to embrace elite consensus, transparency, good governance and local content,” he added. President Tinubu was represented at the inauguration by the Vice President, Kashim Shettima. Other dignitaries that graced the occasion included Bisi Akande and Iyiola Omisore, other All Progressives

item.title: Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. item.title: The best Black Friday deals Ars could find
item.description: Every year has a Prime Day—some years even have two Prime Days!—where we celebrate the life and achievements of the greatest leader the Autobots have ever known: the inimitable Optimus Prime. But just as every dawn is twinned by a dusk that steals its light, so too did Optimus Prime's bright spark fade, extinguished by the foul hand of Megatron during the Great Decepticon Incursion of 2005 . It is a day that lives in infamy forever, and we all know the tale—how the evil Megatron (cursed be the flow of his energon!) commandeered an Autobot shuttle, cruelly murdered its crew, and launched a cowardly surprise attack against Autobot City—a plan utterly bereft of honor, as was so typical of Megatron's schemes. Even as individual Autobots strove to secure Autobot City— heroes, all of them !—hope began to fade under an onslaught that included an attack by the fearsome Devastator , against which there appeared to be no defense. And then, at the precipice of disaster, Optimus Prime made the fateful declaration whose words still ring out to this day: " Megatron must be stopped, no matter the cost ." The fearless Autobot transformed, rolled out, and got the job done—even though that cost was high. Many brave Autobots besides Optimus Prime lost their lives during the fighting. It was truly a dark day, a black day—and so, every year on the Friday after Thanksgiving, we pause to remember the noble sacrifices made by Prime and by so many others. This is why today is known as Black Friday. Read full article Comments

item.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
item.description: null Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper /the Plough. It's gone. Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn. What's happening and when to look Stars move anti-clockwise around the north celestial pole, so Cassiopeia changes orientation. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3. This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations , it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris , the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon. This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract. How and when I'm watching it The names and distances of the stars in Cassiopeia. (Image credit: Starry Night) I'm going to observe Cassiopeia twice on the same evening this week, which is about as complicated as the experiment needs to get. The first time will be shortly after darkness falls. I'll find the W, note which way it seems to be pointing and use something fixed — a rooftop, tree or chimney — to give myself a rough reference for its position. I'll return to my backyard before bed, and see where the pattern ha

item.title: Arteta urges Arsenal not to underestimate troubled Man City
item.description: Mikel Arteta insisted Friday that Arsenal will not underestimate spluttering Manchester City in Sunday’s crucial clash with their Premier League title rivals. Arteta’s leaders are six points clear of third-placed City heading into the showdown at the Emirates Stadium. City led the table in the opening months of the season before suffering a major dip in recent weeks. Enzo Maresca’s men have only won just in their last seven games in all competitions and are without a victory in their last four league matches. Arteta cannot explain City’s stumble but he has no intention of taking three points for granted against them. “I don’t know, that’s a question for them. All I can say is when I watch them play, a lot of the games they have to win they do more than the opponent, but this is football,” the Arsenal manager told reporters on Friday. “When we play the home games against big teams that becomes crucial in the title challenge, we know how important those games are. But the second part, we’re in November, and we still have long to play. “The challenge is for us, we cannot control what other opponents are going to do.” City boss Maresca has been criticised for his team’s poor form but Arteta is a firm admirer of the Italian, who is in his first season in charge after replacing Pep Guardiola. “I know Enzo personally and he’s a phenomenal guy. He lives and breathes football, is very analytical. He is already on the great managerial career already. Everything is super positive,” Arteta said. – Arsenal ‘hunger’ – Arsenal sit top despite also being below their peak form in recent weeks. They were held to draws in their last two games against Newcastle in the Premier League and Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League. Prior to that, the Gunners eked out three wins by a one-goal margin and suffered an embarrassing League Cup exit at fourth-tier Fleetwood. Arteta believes Arsenal are still rounding into form and he hopes the motivation of a valuable victory against City will spur them on as they chase the high of a second successive title. “Yes, more hunger to do it again. To have those moments again together,” he said. “Everybody puts in unbelievable shifts every week, to analyse the opponent, to breathe the right atmosphere around the boys and to win the game, week in, week out.” City’s dynastic run under Guardiola is an inspiration to Arteta even if they have lost their way lately. “You certainly learn from that. And that inspires you to go to a different level, and that’s the level Manchester City brought to this league, because what they have done is unprecedented,” he said. Arteta revealed David Raya is back in training after missing the Dortmund game with a shoulder injury suffered against Newcastle. Kepa Arrizabalaga deputised against Dortmund but Arteta would not reveal if Raya is ready to return to action this weekend. The post Arteta urges Arsenal not to underestimate troubled Man City appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Fury cleared for Joshua fight after wife retracts schizophrenia claim
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Tyson Fury has been cleared to fight Anthony Joshua after passing the required pre-fight medical checks, following controversy over his wife Paris’s comments about his mental health. According to Sky Sports, British Boxing Board of Control general secretary Robert Smith confirmed Fury had passed his medicals ahead of the heavyweight bout at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium on December 11. “Fury cleared last night. All up to date medicals cleared. Promoter told this morning,” Smith said. Paris Fury had said in an initial version of a Netflix documentary that her husband had been diagnosed with schizophrenia. She later clarified that he had never received such a diagnosis and said she had used the word while recalling a conversation from many years ago. “Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis,” she said. Use up and down arrow keys to resize the meta box pane. The boxing board had been investigating the comments and could have refused Fury a licence if it found him unfit to fight. Netflix said it had updated the documentary footage following Paris’s clarification. Use up and down arrow keys to resize the meta box pane. The documentary explores Fury’s experiences with depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder, which became particularly severe after his 2015 victory over Wladimir Klitschko. Fury has also spoken about drug and alcohol addiction and the difficulties he faced during that period. Paris said she was proud of her husband for speaking openly about his experiences and thanked the public for supporting their family. item.title: Stream Detty December From Anywhere: LivDot Brings BNXN, Ruger, Oxlade and Fola Concerts to Global Audiences
item.description: Bada Akintunde-Johnson: MD/CEO Livdot Technologies Liimited. Fans who can’t make it to Lagos this December no longer have to miss it. LivDot , a new live-event streaming platform, will stream concerts by BNXN , Fola , Oxlade and Ruger live and exclusively to audiences worldwide from 19 to 22 December. The launch also rewrites the maths of a sell-out. When a 5,000-capacity concert sells out, the ticketing opportunity usually ends there. On LivDot, the same show can sell 50,000 or more streaming tickets to fans across Nigeria, Africa and the diaspora. LivDot was founded by Bada Akintunde-Johnson , former Country Manager of Paramount Skydance Africa, whose career spans MTV Base, BET, Nickelodeon and Comedy Central in Nigeria. “Imagine being in London, Houston or Toronto and experiencing the energy of Detty December in real time,” said Akintunde-Johnson. “For fans who can’t make the trip, we are curing your fear of missing out by bringing Lagos’s live entertainment to you, wherever you are.” The December lineup Exclusive streams on LivDot this season include: 12 December — The Worship Project by The Fountain of Life Church 19 December — BNXN (formerly known as Buju) 20 December — Fola 21 December — Oxlade 22 December — Ruger 25 December — Saheed Osupa and Friends White Party Date [TBC] — The Digital Product Growth Summit More headline concerts, faith and business events are lined up for the season. Fans can buy streaming tickets or watch free events at www.livdot.co Beyond the venue walls For event organizers, LivDot is the infrastructure behind that extra audience. It brings production, live streaming and payments together in one place, with content distributed free or behind a pay-per-view access fee. A built-in marketplace of vetted photographers and videographers makes hiring quality production talent easier and more consistent. “For too long, the reach and economics of live events have been defined by the walls of the venue,” said Akintunde-Johnson. “A sold-out room should be the floor of an event’s audience and earning potential, not the ceiling.” For artists, it means reaching fans abroad far more often. Instead of waiting for an occasional arena date in London or New York, an artist can stage a lean live performance in Nigeria, sell affordable digital tickets to fans worldwide, and let LivDot handle production, streaming and payment. That opens the door to intimate shows, exclusive sessions, album listenings and other fan experiences. “Artists should be able to perform more often, on their own terms, and earn directly from fans around the world,” Akintunde-Johnson added. “We want to make that commercially practical.” Concerts are only the start. Weddings, birthdays, comedy shows, cultural festivals, fashion shows and conferences all have people who want to be there but can’t. LivDot is expanding partnerships with brands, promoters, artists, event planners and production companies to turn that demand into participation and new revenue. The ven

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 27, 1885: Astronomer captures 1st known photo of a meteor during an Andromedid meteor storm
item.description: null On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor. The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic. The meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower . The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet , which broke apart in the 1850s. When Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm . This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour. The November 1872 incidence of the Andromedid meteor shower, as seen over France, in a painting. (Image credit: Alto Vintage Images/Alamy) Why it mattered Not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible. But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name). Meteor Shower Quiz: How Well Do You Know 'Shooting Stars'? This modern photo of the Geminid meteor shower shows dozens of meteors captured in a long exposure by Josh Drury. Ladislaus Weinek, who captured the first photo of a meteor, had to use a photographic plate in 1889. (Image credit: Josh Dury) Camera technology has come a long way since 1885, which is good since it is a bit harder to see the Andromedids these days. Instead of photographic plates or digital cameras, astronomers now have to use special tracking equipment to record images of Andromedid meteors. In 2011, astronomers announced that the meteor shower seemed to be undergoing a resurgence of activity, with 50 meteors per hour, and upticks were expected in 2018 and 2023. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: It won’t happen again — Fashola on Peter Obi’s 2023 victory in Lagos
item.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has said the All Progressives Congress was caught off guard by Peter Obi’s victory in Lagos during the 2023 presidential election, insisting the party would not allow a repeat in future elections. Obi, who contested on the platform of the Labour Party, defeated APC candidate Bola Tinubu in his home state, securing a narrow victory that stunned the ruling party. Speaking in an exclusive interview with ARISE News, Fashola admitted that the outcome was unexpected, attributing the party’s surprise to pre-election surveys that did not indicate Lagos was at risk. “We were blindsided. It won’t happen again,” he said. Asked whether the APC had underestimated its opponents by taking Lagos for granted, the former governor rejected the suggestion, explaining that the party’s projections had not identified the state as a major battleground. “Lagos didn’t look like a battleground at the time, not from the numbers,” Fashola said. He added, “We do very scientific surveys, and Lagos didn’t look like a battleground in that sense. So that’s why I say I was blindsided, on reflection.” Fashola, however, said the party recovered from the setback shortly after the presidential election, arguing that subsequent electoral outcomes showed it remained politically strong in the state. “In spite of that setback at the presidential election, we turned it around very quickly,” he said. He also dismissed suggestions that Obi’s victory marked a lasting decline in the APC’s influence in Lagos, saying the party should focus on its record and policies rather than dwell on the past. The former governor spoke amid questions about voter intimidation, ethnic rhetoric and violence during the 2023 elections in Lagos, insisting that political competition should not involve threats, attacks or hate speech. Fashola said politicians could aggressively promote their parties and challenge opponents without resorting to personal attacks or inflammatory rhetoric. “You are entitled to very vigorously and vociferously campaign for your party, as I am doing now, and showing what our record is, without damaging anybody’s name, anybody’s reputation, and without hate speech,” he said. He described democracy as a “non-contact sport”, arguing that parties should compete through ideas, policies and performance rather than intimidation or violence. The post It won’t happen again — Fashola on Peter Obi’s 2023 victory in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. More than 11,000 New Yorkers invested, alongside what the state called hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. item.title: Bruno Fernandes misses Man U training ahead of Brentford clash
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes missed the club’s training session on Friday ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford on Saturday, raising concerns over his availability for the encounter. The Portuguese midfielder was absent from the session at Carrington after reportedly feeling slightly unwell. However, his absence was not linked to an injury, with the club opting to rest him as a precaution. According to ESPN, Fernandes is expected to recover in time for Saturday’s fixture at Old Trafford, with manager Mauricio Pochettino hopeful that the midfielder will be available for selection. Fernandes’ absence initially attracted attention after footage released by Manchester United from Friday’s training session showed the team preparing without their captain. The 32 year old remains an important figure in United’s midfield and has recorded six goal involvements in the Premier League this season, scoring four goals and providing two assists. He also comes into the Brentford encounter on the back of an impressive midweek performance, having scored twice in United’s 2-2 Champions League draw against his former club, Sporting. Pochettino will be looking to secure his first victory as United manager after the draw, having previously overseen encouraging performances against Liverpool and Sporting. Brentford, meanwhile, head to Old Trafford in confident mood after recording a convincing 4-0 victory over Everton last weekend. Their manager, Keith Andrews, has also expressed admiration for Pochettino, saying he had followed the Argentine’s teams during his own coaching career. Saturday’s meeting presents Pochettino with another opportunity to claim his first win as United manager, with Fernandes’ possible return expected to provide a significant boost to the hosts. item.title: French student protests: A 'very bizarre' government response
item.description: “The government had a very bizarre way of dealing with the student protests,” says Jean-Rémi Girard, a secondary school teacher and union representative in Asnières-sur-Seine. He explains how teachers sought to defuse tensions by listening to students, and respecting their right to protest, while keeping classes running. He recounts a police intervention last October and the case of a student facing trial for defending a classmate, and has the full support of several teachers. Girard questions the government's heavy-handed policing and largely symbolic proposals on class sizes and university admissions. “There wasn't really a negotiation,” he says, also highlighting the number of education workers injured during the protests.

item.title: Back to Black Friday: 'We are now bombarded with offers throughout the year'
item.description: Black Friday was once a single day of holiday sales, held the day after Thanksgiving. Then retailers began kicking things off a day early, on Thanksgiving itself. “We are now bombarded with offers throughout the year,” says Hilary Ingham, Professor of Economics and Department Head at Lancaster University, who has no plans to shop this Black Friday. Ingham acknowledges a growing sense of “retail fatigue” but still sees the potential for a peak in sales. Meanwhile, an investigation by The Telegraph suggests that six in ten of the most popular products were actually more expensive than earlier in the year, underscoring the need for consumers to remain vigilant and track prices over time.

item.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
item.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. item.title: Artemis III astronauts meet their spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 27, 2026
item.description: null NASA's Artemis III astronauts pose holding up three fingers to symbolize their mission as they visit the Orion spacecraft they will ride to space. (Image credit: NASA/Kim Shiflett) Training for a mission to space is hard work. But sometimes you have to take a minute and have a little fun with your crewmates. What is it? Crowded together with the Orion spacecraft, the four astronauts that make up the Artemis III crew hold up three fingers, taking a brief pause in their rigorous training for some lighthearted crew bonding. In the snapshot , the crew — from left to right, NASA astronauts Randy Bresnick (mission commander) and Frank Rubio (mission specialist), European Space Agency astronaut Luca Parmitano (mission pilot) and NASA astronaut Andre Douglas (mission specialist) — is spotted posing alongside the same Orion spacecraft that they will fly to space as part of their mission. This brief moment of levity took place where the spacecraft currently resides at the Neil A. Armstrong Operations and Checkout Building at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Why is it incredible? This crew has a serious mission ahead of them. The four astronauts will launch to low-Earth orbit around Earth where they plan to practice rendezvous and docking with both Blue Origin and SpaceX's lunar landing vehicles , Blue Moon and Starship, respectively. To prepare, the crew has to undergo months of critical training to both be physically ready while prepared to handle any situation that might come up during their mission. And while Artemis III isn't landing astronauts on the moon, it is a critical step toward that goal. If Artemis III goes to plan and NASA has a lunar landing vehicle that passes rendezvous and docking tests with the Orion spacecraft, Artemis IV might see astronauts land on the moon for the first time since the final Apollo mission in 1972.

item.title: NASA’s NG-25 Mission to Launch Pioneering Space Crops Research
item.description: Experiments in the Ohalo III facility (pictured above) aim to validate plant-water delivery, optimize volume, and advance crop-production research. These insights could inform the design of plant production systems for future deep-space missions. NASA NASA experiments, including a first-of-its-kind space crop production system, will travel to the International Space Station aboard Northrop Grumman’s 25th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency. Investigations from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division will advance research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration, expanding knowledge of space crops and human health. Groundbreaking space crops Astronauts will need sustainable sources of food to travel farther and stay longer in space. To help understand how crop production works in microgravity, NASA is launching a novel space crops experiment . The new prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing safe, nutritious, and reliable crop production systems for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions. Knowledge gained from the space crop production system also could help inform agricultural practices such as vertical farming and indoor growing systems. Researchers will use this investigation to validate the system’s water delivery and volume optimization technology aboard the space station. Tiny brain models aboard station A precision health investigation is the next step toward enabling long-duration studies of human brain tissues in space. The research builds on a previous investigation that sent small, lab-grown models of the human brain, called miBrains, to the space station. This experiment will validate a miniature fluid-handling system designed to mix, deliver, and maintain the nutrient-rich liquid needed to keep the tissues alive. Researchers could use the findings to help identify potential neurological risks associated with spaceflight and develop strategies to protect astronaut health. It also may advance human tissue research and neurological disease modeling on Earth. Biological & Physical Sciences Division NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division pioneers scientific discovery and enables exploration by using space environments to conduct investigations not possible on Earth. Studying biological and physical phenomena under extreme conditions allows researchers to advance the fundamental scientific knowledge required to go farther and stay longer in space, while also benefitting life on Earth.

item.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
item.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. item.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November. The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported , extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets. Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift. Tech futures lead the risk rebound Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.2% by 6:42 a.m. ET, Reuters reported, as investors returned from Thanksgiving and piled back into battered AI-linked shares. Nvidia gained 3.6% in premarket trading, while AMD climbed 4.4% and Broadcom added 3.4%. S&P 500 futures rose 1.6%, and Dow futures gained 1.3%. “There have been some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note cited by Reuters. The S&P 500 is headed for its best week since April, though it remains on course for its worst November since 2008. Bitcoin price has followed that rebound but lagged it. The major U.S. stock indexes are each up around 4% on the week, and silver jumped about 7% to above $44 an ounce on Friday while gold added 2.5% to above $3,670. Stocks close early at 1 p.m. ET, and the bond market shuts at 2 p.m. Rate hike bets and ETF outflows linger The macro backdrop still weighs on the bitcoin price. Traders are almost fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike in December after data this week showed the economy grew faster than first estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated in October, Reuters reported. Third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.84%. Spot bitcoin ETFs are also still losing cash. The U.S. funds lost $453 million on Wednesday, their seventh straight day of outflows, with BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounting for $329.7 million. That pushed November outflows to about $5.39 billion, extending what was already a record month for the funds. Crypto stocks and miners in focus Crypto stocks face their own test in Friday’s short session. Strategy shares rose 3.1% to $79.96 on Wednesday, while Coinbase gained 1.3% to $103.72. Bitcoin miners that have moved into AI hosting tracked the tech rally, with IREN and Cipher Digital each gaining 8% in premarket trading. item.title: Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June Galaxy has withdrawn its October call that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June, saying the technical signal behind it failed after seven straight weeks of losses and that the bear market is “very likely not over.” Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, laid out the reversal in a report published Wednesday and sent to clients a day earlier. “We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June,” the report said. “The signal it rested on has failed.” The firm’s Oct. 26 note had argued that bitcoin had entered an accumulation phase. Galaxy said at the time that a weekly close back below the 50-week moving average that was not regained within a month would invalidate its technical case. That is what happened. Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 8 at $74,968, 0.7% below the 50-week average, after seven weekly closes above it. It then closed the week ended Nov. 15 below the 200-week average, which Galaxy has described as the floor of past bear markets. Galaxy points to $58,525 The week ended Nov. 22 closed at $61,104, 17.9% below the 50-week average and 10.4% below the 200-week average of $68,159. Bitcoin traded below its July 1 intraday low on Nov. 20 and reached $55,100 on Nov. 21, but the June 30 closing low of $58,525 held on a daily basis through Nov. 22. Galaxy now treats that level as the line to watch. A daily close below $58,525 would be “the start of a move to a materially lower low,” the report said, and the firm would not treat such a close as a buying signal by itself. History is not kind to breaks like that. In the seven prior bear market cases where bitcoin closed below a low that had stood for at least 60 days, the eventual low was at least 17% lower, with a median of 52%. Applied to the June low, that works out to about $48,500 and $28,200. Bitcoin briefly slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday morning as the Nasdaq sank, but it ended the day back above $60,000 and has not posted a daily close below $58,525. It traded near $60,800 on Thursday morning. Late by the clock, early by the depth Galaxy said two readings of the market disagree. By the calendar, this bear is old: Nov. 22 was day 412 since the Oct. 6, 2025, record, longer than the 163 to 406 days from high to low in the four prior bear markets. By depth, it looks unfinished. Bitcoin’s 53% decline compares with drops of 77% to 93% in earlier bears. It also has not closed a day below its realized price of $53,205, something every prior bear did for at least 140 days, and only two of the 13 bottom signals Galaxy tracks have been met. “The clock says this bear is overdue to end, the depth says it has further to fall, and we do not believe the price record alone can settle which,” the report said. Flows have not helped. Galaxy estimates U.S. spot bitcoin ETPs hold about 1.24 million BTC, 9.7% below their October 2025 peak, after shedding 71,339 BTC, or $4.95 billion, since Oct. 4. item.title: The Oura Ring 5 just got its biggest discount ever for Black Friday
item.description: The Oura Ring 5 is smaller and more comfortable to wear than the Ring 4 (surprise, surprise). | Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge If you’ve been curious about smart rings but have been put off by their high price tags, Black Friday is a good time to consider giving one a try. That’s because the Oura Ring 5 , which we consider the best smart ring you can buy, has dropped to an all-time low of $299 ($100 off) at Amazon , Best Buy , Walmart , and Oura’s online storefront for Black Friday. Oura Ring 5 Where to Buy: $399 $299 at Amazon $399 $299 at Walmart $399 $299 at Best Buy Compared to the Ring 4 , the Oura Ring 5 offers a thinner, lighter, and more durable design that’s more comfortable to wear throughout the day and while sleeping. Like its predecessor, it can track your sleep, activity, heart rate, and other health metrics, giving you insights into your overall well-being without requiring you to constantly check a screen. It also offers roughly the same battery life and sensors as the prior model, though its new charging case supports wireless charging. (Unfortunately, the case is currently sold separately for $99 .) Oura has also introduced several new software features, including Health Radar, which looks for potentially significant changes in your health. You can also import medical lab results, track GLP-1 medications, and access AI-assisted medical guidance through Oura’s partnership with Counsel Health. My colleague Victoria Song appreciated how the latter makes it easier to connect with an actual doctor, though she found it better suited for quick medical questions than more serious health concerns. However, none of these software features are exclusive to the Ring 5, and you’ll still need a $5.99 monthly Oura membership to access most of its health insights. Given how similar the two generations are, we wouldn’t recommend upgrading if you already own a Ring 4. But if you’re new to smart rings, the current discount makes Oura’s latest model much more attractive, especially since it’s only $50 more than the Ring 4’s starting price. item.title: UK government rejects national consultation on AI datacenters
item.description: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. Briefly, the Covenant tests are that operators cover any energy costs they create, so that communities do not have to pick up the bill; that they invest in local communities; adhere to the highest environmental standards; create jobs and drive reindustrialization; and provide secure and reliable access to their compute resources. If this has a ring of familiarity, it is because President Trump earlier this year introduced a Ratepayer Protection Pledge , under which hyperscalers and AI companies agreed to protect US consumers from any bill shocks due to the energy and infrastructure requirements of their datacenter projects. It seems that where the US leads, the UK still often follows. The Covenant sets out efficiency targets and reporting expectations, but does not explain how compliance will be enforced or specify penalties for failing to meet its tests. Protect the

item.title: [PHOTOS] Adeleke Sworn In For Second Term As Osun Governor
item.description: Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has been sworn in for a second term, beginning another four-year tenure that will run until 2030. Adeleke took the oath of office on Friday, November 27, 2026, at an inauguration ceremony held at the Osogbo Township Stadium. The state Chief Judge administered the oath of office to Deputy Governor Kola Adewusi before swearing in Adeleke. The ceremony was attended by Vice President Kashim Shettima, who led several dignitaries, including former Osun State Governor Bisi Akande, Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa, and former Senate President Bukola Saraki. The entertainment industry was also represented, with Afrobeats singer Davido, alongside B-Red and Shina Rambo, attending the ceremony to celebrate the governor. Adeleke secured re-election in the August 15, 2026 governorship election on the platform of the Accord Party after defecting from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). He polled 511,067 votes to defeat the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, who secured 444,815 votes. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke sworn in as governor for a second term. item.title: Lloyds and Bank of Scotland apps fall over on payday
item.description: Lloyds Bank and Bank of Scotland customers reported problems accessing online banking and transferring money on Friday morning. Reports on Downdetector began rising around 1000 UTC. Lloyds also acknowledged problems on its service status page . A reader who supplied the screenshot below noted the particularly awkward timing: the last Friday of the month is payday for many workers. It's also retail silly season: while Brits don't celebrate Thanksgiving, many UK outlets nonetheless participate in Black Friday sales, meaning storefronts are losing out. Others are concerned with more practical purchases. One customer tweeted that she had "no food at home and cannot shop because I cannot transfer funds from my secondary Lloyds account to my main one. At this point I'm just going to withdraw every penny the moment I'm paid, so much for Internet banking. Never had this years ago." Bank of Scotland, another Lloyds Banking Group brand, reported similar problems on its service status page : " We're aware some customers are having issues with our app and online banking at the moment. We're sorry about this and are working hard to fix it." Earlier this year, a botched overnight software update at Lloyds Banking Group potentially exposed other customers' transaction information to almost 448,000 app users. In a letter to Parliament's Treasury Committee, consumer relationships CEO Jasjyot Singh blamed a defect in the API handling transaction data. The incident affected Lloyds, Halifax, and Bank of Scotland, and prompted goodwill payments to thousands of customers. Lloyds Banking Group said late last year that it had more than 21 million mobile app users and over 23 million digitally active customers. A spokesperson for Lloyds Banking Group told The Register : "We're aware some customers are having difficulty accessing the app this morning. We’re sorry for the inconvenience and are working to get things back to normal as quickly as possible." ®

item.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
item.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®

item.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
item.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. No number of testimonials replaces a written contract that states what you are paying for, what you are not paying for, and what happens if a payment is missed. None of this is complicated. It is just not taught. The i

item.title: Astronomers watch a red giant star greedily devour a stellar 'Bao bun' before erupting: 'We couldn't quite believe our luck'
item.description: null Astronomers witnessed the spectacular cosmic indigestion that resulted from a red giant star that devoured a stellar Bao bun in the form of its smaller companion star. That isn't a random comparison. The cannibal star, which is 350 times bigger than the sun, is nicknamed "Big Bao," while its unfortunate companion had the nickname "Little Bao." The cute cosmic monikers come from the fact that this destructive merger event has been designated AT2025abao. A Bao bun might be a little snack for a human, but this red giant star made a real meal out of Little Bao. This cannibalistic event was tracked by a wide array of ground- and space-based telescopes, including NASA space missions NEOWISE, SPHEREx, and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), as well as the W. M. Keck Observatory in Hawaii. The conclusion of the event AT2025abao was marked by a massive eruption witnessed in Oct. 2025 by two instruments at Caltech's Palomar Observatory: the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) and the Wide-field INfrared Transient ExploreR (WINTER). "The excitement was real," team member Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. "We couldn't quite believe our luck. With detailed observations for several years before the merger, for the first time, we now have an unprecedented glimpse of the conditions that lead to such cosmic events." Reconstructing a violent cosmic collision The story of AT2025abao began when astronomers detected a bright flash in the nearby Andromeda galaxy , a region where scientists hadn't expected to see a cosmic explosion. Responding to this unexpected flash, Karambelkar and colleagues set about investigating its cause with a plethora of telescopes. This led to them seeing a slow and continuous brightening over the course of two years, They determined the cause of the flash was a rare stellar merger, the luminous red nova now designated AT2025abao. They linked this to a star called WNTR23bzdiq / WTP19aalzlk that had been observed steadily brightening since 2019 after being stable for the preceding 30 years. Thus, the team determined that at the heart of the event is a red giant, a star that puffs out to hundreds of times its original size after it runs out of hydrogen in its core. The team theorizes that Big Bao, with a mass seven times greater than the sun, expanded so rapidly and violently that it swallowed its smaller companion star. The unfortunate star, Little Bao, then spiraled into Big Bao's core in fewer than 10 orbits. "A couple of years back, we discovered a star that was gradually brightening. We took a closer look to discover a red giant, or a star that has started to expand toward the end of its life, just like our sun will one day," Karambelkar said. "Steady brightening was unusual, but even if something was stirring, no one expected to see an explosion in their lifetime, as these stars remain relatively stable for thousands of years." item.title: AI boom leaves network operators waiting up to 18 months for kit
item.description: The AI building boom is driving up optical networking equipment prices and stretching delivery times to as much as 18 months, according to network operator RETN. RETN says that network operators and telcos are now directly competing with AI datacenters for chips and other components. As Reg readers will be aware, memory prices have soared by four or five times over the past year or so, but RETN says optical networking equipment prices have risen by around 50 percent since the start of 2026. Worse are the extended delivery times, with optical network kit that used to arrive within three months now taking 12 to 15, and some orders taking up to 18 months. This is as bad as, if not worse than, the shortages during the pandemic, when chip supply problems left network vendors unable to fulfill orders . The issue now is that because of the AI boom, demand is outpacing supplies. In its report, "AI, Connected," RETN says developers building outside established datacenter hubs may need to involve network carriers two to five years before opening. The sudden demand for network kit from hyperscalers and AI campuses is only one factor, RETN says. Raw material shortages, skilled labor shortages, energy constraints, geopolitical tensions, and logistical challenges are also compounding the issue. However, it concedes that many carriers didn't help themselves by previously postponing network upgrades to cut expenditure. That work has now become unavoidable at the worst possible time. Network diversity is now seen as a must-have, the report says. Where customers were once satisfied with two routes to long-haul destinations, they expect operators to provide four or more redundant routes now. The aim is to prevent a single failure from taking down critical services. Multiple connections are only useful protection if they avoid shared physical failure points, such as the same ducts or cable routes. A diverse circuit might cost €1,800 ($1,975) a month instead of €600 ($658), it claims, but an outage could prove far more costly. RETN also says AI datacenters are moving away from populated areas to remote locations, where access to suitable land, power and water may be easier to come by. Hyperscalers are building in the Nordics, where land is affordable, the climate is cooler, and plenty of renewable energy is available. Remote sites may lack the fiber infrastructure needed to connect them to other datacenters and customers. The Register reported on this issue earlier this year. For sites close to cities, developers often fund the fiber themselves, which adds just a few percent to the total project cost. But over longer distances, the case becomes harder to make, and carriers are understandably reluctant to build a long-haul route to serve a single remote site. Some developers are prepared to swallow the cost: RETN says a major cloud provider is exploring converting an abandoned factory in Central Europe into a large-scale server farm, despite little existing fiber in t

item.title: British social security system techies yank services offline following 'cyber incident'
item.description: The UK's Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) has taken some services offline after detecting a "cyber incident," but says regular benefit and pension payments are unaffected. The department announced the precautionary shutdown on Friday morning. "We have taken some DWP online services offline as a precaution after we identified a cyber incident affecting our systems," it said. "We are working closely with the National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre (GC3) to investigate and to bring services back online as quickly as possible and to minimize any disruption. "Regular benefit and pension payments are not affected and will be paid as normal. If an online service you need is unavailable, please try again later. As always, we will never message you to ask for bank details or ask you to click on links." The Register contacted both the DWP and NCSC for more information. The DWP declined to comment beyond the statement issued publicly. GC3 coordinates responses to incidents affecting government. The Government Cyber Unit leads the wider Government Cyber Action Plan, backed by more than £210 million. It is led by the government CISO, Bella Powell. Officials have not commented on any of the usual details one would expect from a cyber incident disclosure, including the specific services that were downed, when they are expected to return, or whether any data is thought to be compromised, even at this early stage. The UK government has also been criticized recently for investing heavily in AI cyber defenses, while the issue of legacy and aging IT continues to be neglected in the background. It announced at the end of October that it was throwing £130 million at AI cyber defense technology , as part of a wider £600 million cross-government AI spending spree announced by the Treasury. ExfilSquad recently claimed to have stolen around 607,000 records from the Department for Education and another 114,000 from the Police National Legal Database. ®
